did_you_know.text: Did you know? All the tribes of Israel came to David at Hebron and declared their kinship with him: “We are your own flesh and blood.”
Did you know? The elders of Israel reminded David that even during Saul’s reign, he was the leader who led Israel, and that the LORD had said to him: “You will shepherd my people.”
Did you know? David was made king over Israel as part of a covenant that the elders of Israel made with him at Hebron before the LORD; afterward, they anointed him king.
Did you know? David was thirty years old when he began to reign, and he reigned for a total of forty years.
Did you know? David reigned over Judah in Hebron for seven years and six months, and then reigned in Jerusalem for thirty-three years over all Israel and Judah.
Did you know? After conquering the stronghold of Zion, David called it “the City of David”; thus Jerusalem became the center of his kingdom.
Did you know? Hiram king of Tyre helped David build his palace and sent him cedar logs, carpenters, and stoneworkers.
Did you know? From the success of his reign, David understood that the LORD had established him as king over Israel and exalted his kingdom “for the sake of his people Israel.”
Did you know? When the Philistines heard that David had been anointed king over Israel, they went up in search of him, and David went down to the stronghold.
Did you know? Before the first battle against the Philistines, David inquired of the LORD and received instructions to go into battle; the victory took place at Baal Perazim.
Did you know? After their defeat at Baal Perazim, the Philistines abandoned their idols, and David and his men carried them away.
Did you know? In the second battle, the LORD commanded David not to attack the Philistines by the same route, but to go around them and come at them opposite the balsam trees.
Did you know? The sound of marching in the tops of the balsam trees was a sign for David to begin the attack, because it meant that the LORD had gone out before him to strike the Philistine camp.
